claims.text: The FeCoNiCrAl feedstock has a particle-size range of 15–45 μm.
A coaxial argon shroud suppresses premature oxidation during atmospheric plasma spraying.
A coaxial argon shroud enhances particle splat formation.
Optimizing the argon shroud will produce a 60–80 μm-thick FeCoNiCrAl bond coat from the standard 15–45 μm feedstock.
The proposed intervention will maintain low as-sprayed oxidation and coating integrity.
An initial argon-shroud flow range of approximately 10–20 L/min can reduce oxygen exposure while maintaining plasma characteristics.
Reduced surface oxidation enhances particle deformability and splat formation.
Enhanced splat formation improves adhesion and layer buildup during deposition.
The inert argon shroud reduces the exposure of in-flight particles to atmospheric oxygen.
Reduced oxygen exposure preserves in-flight particle temperature.
Reduced oxygen exposure preserves the chemical integrity of in-flight particles.
Reduced premature oxidation improves molten-particle wetting and impact dynamics.
Improved wetting and impact dynamics increase coating buildup without compromising bond-coat microstructural integrity.
The unshrouded baseline process produces a 15–45 μm-thick FeCoNiCrAl bond coat.
The unshrouded baseline coating has minimal as-sprayed oxidation.
A 15–45 μm-thick baseline bond coat is insufficient for optimal thermal-barrier-coating performance.
The intervention should remain effective at stand-off distances of 80–100 mm and substrate preheating near 200°C, provided the shroud does not disrupt or excessively cool the plasma jet.
The resulting bond coat will retain suitable integrity under high-temperature thermal cycling in a thermal barrier coating system.
An improperly tuned argon shroud can disrupt the plasma plume or cool particles too rapidly.
Plume disruption or excessive particle cooling can reduce deposition efficiency despite reducing oxidation.
